description: Q-OPTIMA builds an AI satellite disaster intelligence system converting Earth data into actionable triage. Led by Aniket Deo (AI Architect), the team—Sunil Khatri (Data), Loukik Salvi (ML), Abhijeet Jadhav (UI/Dashboard), and Prashant Narayane (Research)—unifies image processing, automated damage detection, and decision support into an operational response platform.
summary: Planetary Pulse is an interactive geospatial analytics platform developed by Team Q-OPTIMA that transforms multi-decadal NASA Earth observation datasets into statistically verified environmental trend intelligence. Global climate drivers frequently produce opposing regional effects—such as accelerated Arctic warming paired with subpolar North Atlantic cooling, or Boreal forest greening alongside Amazonian canopy browning. Raw satellite visualizations alone cannot distinguish true directional climate shifts from short-term natural variability. Our system ingests time-series measurements across NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO, Terra/Aqua MODIS, and Aqua AIRS missions, executing real-time non-parametric Mann-Kendall hypothesis tests (p < 0.05) and Theil-Sen median slope estimations. Through a dual-region divergence interface, scientists, policymakers, and citizens can visualize what is changing, pinpoint where opposing trends emerge, quantify annual rates of change, and verify statistical significance in seconds.
details:
What It Does & How It Works: Planetary Pulse is a browser-based Earth system trend analytics platform designed to answer four core scientific questions: what is changing, where is it changing, how fast is it changing, and is the change statistically significant?

1. Multi-Mission NASA Data Ingestion: The platform synthesizes multi-decadal (2003–2025) Earth observation records across three primary physical domains:

- Hydrosphere & Cryosphere: Terrestrial Water Storage anomalies (cm liquid water equivalent) from NASA GRACE and GRACE-FO.

- Biosphere: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from Terra/Aqua MODIS (MOD13A2).

- Atmosphere & Ocean: Surface air temperature anomalies from NASA Aqua AIRS and GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP).

2. Non-Parametric Statistical Significance Engine: Environmental time series often exhibit non-normal distributions and seasonal autocorrelation. Instead of relying solely on simple linear regression, Planetary Pulse computes:

- Mann-Kendall Trend Test: Evaluates monotonic upward or downward trends and derives exact Z-scores and two-tailed p-values against a strict α = 0.05 significance threshold.

- Theil-Sen Median Slope Estimator: Calculates the robust median rate of change per year, resistant to extreme single-year weather outliers (such as strong El Niño spikes).

3. Opposing Regional Divergence Mode: A defining feature of Earth's interconnected climate system is that a single global forcing mechanism drives opposite regional outcomes. Our side-by-side comparison mode allows users to inspect contrasting teleconnections simultaneously—such as Arctic Polar Amplification (+0.10 °C/yr warming) versus the Subpolar North Atlantic "Cold Blob" (-0.04 °C/yr cooling driven by freshwater meltwater influx), or Boreal forest greening versus Southern Amazonian drought browning.

Tools, Technologies & Architecture

- Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), and Chart.js for interactive multi-series rendering.

- Statistical Backend / Prototype Engine: Python (FastAPI, NumPy) ported to pure client-side JavaScript for zero-latency cloud deployment on GitHub Pages.

Intended Impact & Creativity

By pairing accessible visual storytelling with rigorous non-parametric hypothesis testing, Planetary Pulse bridges the gap between raw NASA Earthdata archives and actionable climate literacy—enabling researchers, educators, and local planners to separate statistically proven climate shifts from natural variability.
